questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless genital ulcer with indurated edges and a clean base. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged, firm, and non-tender. Dark-field microscopy reveals motile spirochetes. What is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Hunterian chancre) caused by Treponema pallidum is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose. This is the drug of choice as per WHO/CDC guidelines.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a chronic ulcerated plaque on the dorsum of the foot with multiple sinuses discharging pale granules. KOH mount shows large fungal elements within the grains. The triad of tumefaction, sinuses, and grains is most consistent with:
questions.exp: The classic triad of tumefaction, sinuses, and discharge of grains defines mycetoma. Eumycetoma is caused by true fungi (e.g., Madurella mycetomatis producing black grains, Pseudallescheria boydii producing white grains). Treatment is long-term itraconazole with surgical debulking.

questions.q: A 45-year-old leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden fever, new erythematous nodules over both arms and legs, and acute neuritis with nerve tenderness. He had similar episodes twice before. This reaction is best managed with:
opts: Continue MDT only without additional therapy
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL, Type 2 lepra reaction) is an immune-complex mediated reaction occurring in BL/LL patients. Thalidomide is the drug of choice for ENL (especially recurrent/chronic) due to its anti-TNF-alpha activity. Prednisolone is used when thalidomide is contraindicated (women of childbearing age). Clofazimine is added for chronic ENL.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on erythematous skin over the trunk and flexures. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone. ELISA detects antibodies against BP180. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid is caused by IgG autoantibodies against BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230 hemidesmosomal proteins. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ (lamina lucida level). Tense bullae with negative Nikolsky sign distinguish it from pemphigus. EBA targets type VII collagen (anchoring fibrils).

questions.q: A 42-year-old woman with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, calcinosis, sclerodactyly, and multiple mat telangiectasias. Which autoantibody is most specifically associated with this pattern?
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibody (ACA) is found in 60–80% of limited cutaneous SSc (lcSSc/CREST syndrome). Anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc (dcSSc) and pulmonary fibrosis. Anti-RNA polymerase III is associated with dcSSc and scleroderma renal crisis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old HIV-positive man (CD4 count 60 cells/μL) develops multiple umbilicated pearly papules on the face. Which statement about this condition in the HIV setting is correct?
opts: Lesions may be large (giant molluscum >1 cm) and numerous, reflecting severe immunosuppression
Treatment with topical acyclovir is curative
The causative virus belongs to the herpesvirus family
CD4 count is not related to disease severity
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum (MCV, a poxvirus) in profoundly immunosuppressed HIV patients (CD4 <100) presents with atypical, numerous, or giant lesions (>1 cm). ART is the most important intervention. Acyclovir has no activity against poxviruses. Severity inversely correlates with CD4 count.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the lower lip after a febrile illness. He has had 8 similar episodes in the past year. The best long-term management strategy is:
opts: Suppressive antiviral therapy with acyclovir 400 mg twice daily
Episodic acyclovir 200 mg five times daily for 5 days only when lesions appear
Topical penciclovir cream applied at prodrome
questions.exp: For patients with >6 recurrences per year of herpes labialis, long-term suppressive acyclovir 400 mg BD reduces recurrence by 70–80%. Suppressive therapy is preferred over episodic therapy for frequent recurrences. Topical agents are less effective and do not prevent recurrence.

questions.q: Skin biopsy of a vulval lesion shows large cells with pale cytoplasm and eccentric nuclei dispersed throughout the epidermis without forming nests. PAS stain and mucicarmine are positive. CEA is expressed. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Extramammary Paget's disease (EMPD) shows large Paget cells with pale cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli, and mucin production in the epidermis. PAS+, mucicarmine+, and CEA+ distinguish it from melanoma (S100+, HMB-45+) and Bowen's disease. EMPD commonly occurs on the vulva, perianal area, and scrotum.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a 3 cm pearly nodule with surface telangiectasias, a rolled border, and central ulceration on the nose. Mohs micrographic surgery is preferred over wide local excision because:
opts: It examines 100% of surgical margins, minimising recurrence while conserving normal tissue on the face
It is faster and less expensive than conventional surgery
It avoids the need for local anaesthesia
It is the only method suitable for treatment of BCC on the nose
questions.exp: Mohs surgery uses horizontal (en face) frozen sections to examine 100% of the surgical margins (peripheral and deep) in real time, allowing complete tumour clearance with maximal tissue conservation. It is indicated for high-risk BCC on the face (H-zone), recurrent tumours, large lesions, and aggressive histological subtypes (morphoeic).

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with well-defined erythematous plaques with silver-white scales on the elbows, knees, and scalp. On removing the scale, pinpoint bleeding is observed. The histological hallmark of this condition is:
opts: Munro microabscesses (neutrophils in stratum corneum) with suprapapillary thinning and elongated rete ridges
Spongiosis with vesicle formation and perivascular eosinophilic infiltrate
Lichenoid band-like infiltrate at the DEJ with Civatte body formation
Granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid cells and Langhans giant cells
questions.exp: Psoriasis histology: acanthosis with regular elongated rete ridges, parakeratosis with retained nuclei, Munro microabscesses (neutrophil collections in corneal layer), suprapapillary plate thinning, dilated tortuous dermal papillary capillaries (causing Auspitz sign on scale removal), and absent granular layer.

questions.q: A term neonate is born encased in a shiny, taut, parchment-like membrane with ectropion and eclabium. The membrane cracks and peels within the first two weeks. This 'collodion baby' phenotype is most commonly associated with which ichthyosis?
questions.exp: Collodion baby is most commonly a presentation of lamellar ichthyosis (due to TGM1 mutations in ~30% of cases) or non-bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma. After shedding, lamellar ichthyosis shows large, plate-like dark scales. X-linked ichthyosis (steroid sulfatase deficiency) does not present as a collodion baby.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on dapsone develops sudden severe back pain, jaundice, and haemoglobinuria 2 weeks after starting therapy. His Hb drops from 12 to 6 g/dL. The peripheral smear shows bite cells and Heinz bodies. The likely cause is:
opts: Dapsone-induced haemolysis in a G6PD-deficient patient
questions.exp: Dapsone causes oxidative haemolysis in all patients dose-dependently, but is severe and acute in G6PD-deficient patients. Heinz bodies (denatured Hb precipitates) and bite cells are hallmarks of G6PD-related haemolysis. Dapsone hydroxylamine metabolite oxidises Hb. G6PD screening before dapsone therapy is recommended.

questions.q: A 17-year-old girl with severe nodulocystic acne is started on isotretinoin. She must be counselled about teratogenicity. The most characteristic malformation caused by isotretinoin embryopathy is:
opts: Microtia/anotia and craniofacial abnormalities (retrognathia, cleft palate)
questions.exp: Isotretinoin (13-cis-retinoic acid) is Category X teratogen. It causes a characteristic embryopathy: craniofacial defects (microtia/anotia, micrognathia, cleft palate), CNS abnormalities (hydrocephalus, cerebellar hypoplasia), cardiovascular defects (conotruncal), and thymic aplasia. Risk is highest in first trimester. Mandatory contraception and pregnancy testing are required.

questions.q: A 50-year-old diabetic woman presents with white, opaque, crumbling toenails with subungual hyperkeratosis involving all 10 toenails. KOH shows septate hyphae. Culture grows Trichophyton rubrum. The best treatment for total dystrophic onychomycosis is:
opts: Oral terbinafine 250 mg daily for 12 weeks (fingernails) or 16–24 weeks (toenails)
Topical amorolfine nail lacquer alone for 6 months
Oral fluconazole 150 mg once weekly indefinitely
Surgical nail avulsion followed by topical antifungal
questions.exp: Terbinafine is the drug of choice for dermatophyte onychomycosis (most common cause: T. rubrum). Terbinafine 250 mg/day for 16–24 weeks is required for toenail involvement. It is fungicidal against dermatophytes (inhibits squalene epoxidase). Topical agents alone are insufficient for total dystrophic onychomycosis.

questions.q: Under Wood's lamp (365 nm), tinea capitis caused by Microsporum canis shows which fluorescence colour?
questions.exp: Microsporum canis and M. audouinii (ectothrix infections) fluoresce bright green under Wood's lamp due to pteridine metabolites. Trichophyton species causing endothrix infections (T. tonsurans, T. violaceum) do NOT fluoresce. T. schoenleinii (favus) shows dull greenish/yellowish fluorescence. Erythrasma (Corynebacterium) shows coral red.

questions.q: A 20-year-old returns from a beach holiday with a serpiginous, erythematous, intensely pruritic track on the dorsum of the right foot advancing 2–3 cm per day. The most effective treatment is:
opts: Topical thiabendazole applied twice daily for 5 days
Oral mebendazole 100 mg BD for 3 days
questions.exp: Cutaneous larva migrans (creeping eruption) is caused by Ancylostoma braziliense larvae migrating in the epidermis. Oral ivermectin 200 μg/kg single dose is the treatment of choice (>95% cure rate). Oral albendazole 400 mg/day for 3–7 days is an alternative. Topical thiabendazole is messy, less effective, and not commercially available in many countries.

questions.q: A 68-year-old chronic smoker presents with yellowish, thickened, wrinkled, lax skin with deep furrows on the posterior neck (cutis rhomboidalis nuchae) and comedones around the eyes. This is:
opts: Favre-Racouchot syndrome (nodular elastosis with cysts and comedones)
questions.exp: Favre-Racouchot syndrome is severe actinic (solar) elastosis on the periorbital area with large open and closed comedones. It is associated with chronic UV exposure and smoking. Histology shows massive accumulation of abnormal elastotic material (elastosis) in the dermis. Treatment includes tretinoin cream and comedone extraction.

questions.q: A 5-year-old boy presents with intensely pruritic, flexural eczema involving the antecubital and popliteal fossae, elevated total IgE (2400 IU/mL), and a personal history of allergic rhinitis. The SCORAD index is 38. The most appropriate step-up therapy at this point is:
opts: Topical tacrolimus 0.03% ointment to the flexural areas
questions.exp: Topical calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus 0.03% for children <2 years, 0.1% for adults; pimecrolimus 1% for mild-moderate) are second-line agents for atopic dermatitis, used on sensitive areas (face, flexures) where topical steroids may cause atrophy. Potent steroids and systemic agents are reserved for severe refractory disease.

questions.q: During standard patch testing for allergic contact dermatitis, a reaction graded '++' (ICDRG grading) at D4 shows:
opts: Intense erythema, coalescing vesicles, and ulceration
questions.exp: ICDRG patch test grading: ? = doubtful (faint erythema only), + = erythema + infiltration + possible papules (weak positive), ++ = erythema + infiltration + papules + vesicles (strong positive), +++ = intense reaction with coalescing vesicles, bullae, or ulceration (extreme positive). Reading at D2 and D4 is standard.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with bilateral parotid enlargement, xerostomia, keratoconjunctivitis sicca, and leukocytoclastic vasculitis is found to have anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies. The most common cutaneous vasculitis in Sjögren's syndrome is:
questions.exp: Waldenström's hypergammaglobulinaemic purpura is the most common vasculitis in primary Sjögren's syndrome, presenting as non-inflammatory palpable purpura on the lower extremities. It results from polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia with immune complex deposition. Anti-Ro/SSA is the hallmark antibody of pSS.

questions.q: A 27-year-old man receives co-trimoxazole for a UTI and develops painful erythema, blistering, and sheet-like skin detachment involving 35% BSA along with extensive mucosal erosions of the eyes, mouth, and genitalia within 2 weeks. The pathological mechanism is:
opts: Drug-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-mediated keratinocyte apoptosis via Fas/FasL and perforin/granzyme B pathway
Type I IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation
Type III immune-complex deposition in dermal vessels
questions.exp: TEN (skin detachment >30% BSA) is a severe drug hypersensitivity reaction mediated by drug-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes. These cells release perforin/granzyme B and express FasL, inducing widespread keratinocyte apoptosis. Sulfonamides (co-trimoxazole) are among the most common triggers. Treatment involves stopping the offending drug and supportive care in a burns unit.

questions.q: A 27-year-old woman presents with intensely pruritic grouped papulovesicles symmetrically distributed over the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Biopsy shows neutrophilic microabscesses at dermal papillary tips with subepidermal vesicle formation. DIF shows granular IgA deposits at the dermoepidermal junction. The most effective long-term management is:
opts: Strict gluten-free diet (primary treatment) plus dapsone for symptomatic relief
Dapsone alone lifelong without dietary restriction
Systemic prednisolone 40 mg/day tapering over 3 months
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is the cutaneous manifestation of gluten-sensitive enteropathy. Granular IgA at dermal papillae on DIF is pathognomonic. A strict gluten-free diet is the primary disease-modifying treatment (reduces IgA deposits over years). Dapsone provides rapid symptomatic relief but does not treat the underlying intestinal disease. Both are required.

questions.q: A borderline lepromatous (BL) leprosy patient treated with MB-MDT for 6 months develops an acute Type 1 (reversal) reaction with new nerve involvement and fresh skin lesions. The most critical reason for prompt aggressive corticosteroid therapy is:
opts: Prevention of irreversible nerve damage and disability
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) lepra reaction is a cell-mediated immune response that causes acute neuritis. Without prompt corticosteroid therapy (prednisolone 40–60 mg/day), irreversible nerve damage with motor and sensory deficits occurs. MDT must be continued alongside steroids. The primary goal is nerve preservation, not lesion clearance.

questions.q: A 30-year-old pregnant woman (36 weeks gestation) develops intensely pruritic urticarial papules and plaques in the abdominal striae with sparing of the umbilicus. She is primigravid. Fetal outcome in this condition is:
opts: Normal fetal outcome; condition is benign and self-limiting
Increased risk of fetal growth restriction
High risk of fetal transmission of the dermatosis
Risk of preterm delivery due to associated cholestasis
questions.exp: Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy (PEP/PUPPP) is the most common specific dermatosis of pregnancy (incidence 1:160), typically occurring in third-trimester primigravidas. It starts in the striae, spares the umbilicus, and has no adverse fetal or maternal outcome. It resolves spontaneously after delivery. Management is symptomatic (topical steroids, antihistamines).

questions.q: A 21-year-old presents with perifollicular haemorrhages, 'corkscrew' hairs, bleeding gums, and impaired wound healing. He has lived on processed food for months with minimal fresh fruits. The skin lesion is due to deficiency of which cofactor essential for collagen hydroxylation?
questions.exp: Scurvy (Vitamin C deficiency) presents with perifollicular haemorrhages, 'corkscrew' or 'swan-neck' hairs, bleeding gums, hyperkeratosis, and impaired wound healing. Ascorbic acid is the essential cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase enzymes that hydroxylate proline and lysine in collagen, necessary for triple helix formation and cross-linking.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman undergoes fractional CO2 laser resurfacing for acne scars. The most important post-procedure instruction to prevent the most common complication is:
opts: Strict sun avoidance and broad-spectrum sunscreen to prevent post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH)
Vigorous cleansing of treated areas twice daily
questions.exp: Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH) is the most common complication of laser resurfacing, especially in Fitzpatrick skin types IV–VI. Strict photoprotection with broad-spectrum SPF 50+ sunscreen, sun avoidance, and pre/post-treatment skin lightening agents (hydroquinone) are essential. Premature retinoid use can impair wound healing.

questions.q: A 14-year-old girl with recurrent furunculosis is found to have a neutrophil oxidative burst defect on DHR flow cytometry (absent oxidative burst). Nitroblue tetrazolium (NBT) test is negative. The underlying condition is:
opts: Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD) — deficiency of NADPH oxidase
Chediak-Higashi syndrome — deficiency of lysosomal trafficking regulator
Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) — deficiency of CD18
Job syndrome (HIES) — STAT3 mutation with elevated IgE
questions.exp: Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD) is caused by mutations in NADPH oxidase complex components (most commonly CYBB on X chromosome in males; autosomal in females). Phagocytes cannot produce reactive oxygen species to kill catalase-positive organisms (S. aureus, Aspergillus). NBT test (fails to turn blue) and DHR flow cytometry (absent oxidative burst) are diagnostic.

questions.q: A 48-year-old man presents with violaceous flat-topped polygonal papules on the wrists, ankles, and buccal mucosa (Wickham's striae). Histology shows a dense band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the DEJ, saw-tooth rete ridges, and eosinophilic globules in the lower epidermis. Hepatitis C serology is positive. These globules represent:
questions.exp: Lichen planus histology: hypergranulosis, hyperkeratosis, irregular 'saw-tooth' acanthosis, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the DEJ (interface dermatitis), basal vacuolar degeneration, and Civatte bodies (eosinophilic round structures = apoptotic/necrotic keratinocytes, also called colloid or hyaline bodies). LP is strongly associated with HCV infection.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with bilateral, symmetric brownish-grey hyperpigmentation on the malar area that worsens with sun exposure and during pregnancy. Wood's lamp shows enhancement of the pigmentation. The most likely type and the line of treatment is:
opts: Epidermal melasma; triple combination cream (hydroquinone 4% + tretinoin 0.05% + fluocinolone acetonide 0.01%) + SPF 50+ sunscreen
Dermal melasma; Q-switched Nd:YAG laser 1064 nm alone
Mixed melasma; topical azelaic acid 20% alone for 6 months
Epidermal melasma; oral tranexamic acid 250 mg BD alone
questions.exp: Wood's lamp enhancement indicates epidermal melanin deposition (epidermal melasma). The gold-standard treatment is the triple combination cream (modified Kligman's formula) combined with strict broad-spectrum photoprotection. Oral tranexamic acid is an adjunct. Dermal melasma does not enhance under Wood's lamp and responds poorly to topical agents.

questions.q: A 23-year-old sexually active man presents with multiple soft, painless flesh-coloured cauliflower-like perianal growths. Biopsy shows koilocytes (cells with perinuclear halo and wrinkled nuclei). The HPV types most commonly responsible for benign anogenital warts are:
questions.exp: Condylomata acuminata (anogenital warts) are caused by HPV types 6 and 11 (low-risk, non-oncogenic). HPV 16/18 are high-risk oncogenic types associated with anogenital carcinomas and cervical cancer. Koilocytes are the cytopathic hallmark of HPV infection on histology. The nonavalent HPV vaccine covers types 6, 11, 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, and 58.
